entries.title: An expired lease cannot authorize terminal cancellation
entries.trigger: a worker holds a queue lease and reads a payload before performing external work.
entries.mechanism: payload lookup returned nothing after lease expiry; a fallback cancellation checked only the old lease ID and permanently discarded still-valid delivery.
entries.prevention: interpret empty reads according to their contract. Require current lease ownership for terminal cancellation, so another worker can reclaim unfinished work. Do not infer entity deletion from an expired authorization window. Keep provider acceptance and retry ambiguity explicit.
verification: expire the lease between claim and payload read; call cancellation, reclaim the row and complete it. Preserve ordinary live-lease cancellation and exact replacement-lease checks.
boundaries: 2026-09-07, PostgreSQL 17 queue RPCs; applicability depends on the queue's lease contract.

entries.title: Owner-gated affordances need authoritative remote identity
entries.trigger: a server-backed interaction is intentionally owner-only while its optional local owner record can be missing, stale or not yet restored.
entries.mechanism: a social control trusted only a merged local `isOwn` projection. A remote shared entities displayed the current author's username but lost its owner long-press action; the same hold then completed as an ordinary tap and changed reaction state.
entries.prevention: when the product contract is owner-only, carry the remote author ID to the interaction boundary and compare it with the current account-scoped actor ID. Keep the trusted server command owner-only; client recognition controls only affordance visibility and cannot replace authorization.
verification: render a remote current-author entity with `isOwn=false`, then prove the owner action is exposed, its long press does not invoke the ordinary tap, and an unmatched actor remains private. Repeat on the affected device against the hosted authorization boundary.
boundaries: 2026-09-12, React Native 0.86.3 and React 19.2; source regression and physical-device hosted owner and empty-state paths pass. A later product change removed the incident's owner-only rule; the lesson remains applicable to interactions that retain such a gate. Tactile, iOS, and assistive-technology acceptance remain separate.

entries.title: Provider cleanup belongs to the registration that was sent
entries.trigger: a provider may report an invalid push token after that token is registered again.
entries.mechanism: deleting by token, or token plus account, removes a newer valid registration. The same account and Auth session can register the same token again while an older send is pending.
entries.prevention: capture the registration incarnation when preparing delivery, persist it with the provider ticket, and match it atomically during cleanup. Legacy outcomes without that identity cannot safely delete the current binding. Keep provider payloads free of internal ownership fields.
verification: delayed invalid-token results after another account, another sign-in and same-session re-registration; unchanged-target controls; both real registration/delete lock orders; lost completion response and retry. Physical delivery is separate from database ownership proof.
boundaries: 2026-09-07, Expo Push HTTP API and PostgreSQL 17 with real Auth/RPC and concurrency fixtures.

entries.title: Logout must fence late registration by sign-in identity
entries.trigger: one installation rebinds a push token between accounts, including offline logout.
entries.mechanism: a server registration outlived its lost response and overwrote the next account's binding. Actor identity alone also cannot distinguish a later sign-in by the same person.
entries.prevention: persist the initiating session's cleanup intent before dispatch, finish its revocation before replacing the receipt, and bind the request to that exact checked authorization. Server cleanup must fence both entered and not-yet-arrived work. Use supported Auth session identity; JWT validity or request cancellation alone does not establish that logout completed remotely.
verification: hold a real registration, log out and hand off, then release and replay it. Cover an unknown first response, offline Auth, a new sign-in by the same actor, another installation, refresh and late SQLite cleanup. State precisely which guarantees require an updated client receipt.
boundaries: 2026-09-07, Supabase Auth/JS 2.112.3, local PostgreSQL concurrency, real Auth/HTTP and SQLite. Native delivery and released-client acceptance require their own evidence.

entries.title: Every projection must enforce current access before pagination
entries.trigger: a notification, activity feed or summary projects an entity whose audience can change.
entries.mechanism: entity reads and unread summary hid a former friend's item, while a separate inbox RPC still exposed its activity and consumed the first page slot. Eventual pruning was too late.
entries.prevention: reuse the canonical current-visibility predicate in each trusted projection before LIMIT/cursor pagination. Keep recipient isolation and installed-client contracts. Async cleanup and client filtering cannot substitute for authorization at the read boundary.
verification: create real activity, revoke access, then compare entity, summary, inbox and delivery preparation. Prove the read is correct before cleanup runs. Preserve current-member, public/own, cursor, legacy-client and raw-identity privacy controls; check cross-device refresh separately.
boundaries: 2026-09-07, PostgreSQL 17 / Supabase RPC with transactional and real HTTP regressions.

entries.title: Auth mutations participate in teardown
entries.trigger: a persisted SDK session and account-specific local cleanup share one installation.
entries.mechanism: email/profile updates can persist a session after a delayed response, just as sign-in can. A challenge can also finish after its originating account or screen has gone away.
entries.prevention: check operation ownership before dispatch after every external interaction. Include entered SDK session mutations in the account teardown barrier and reject new work during cleanup. Verify pinned SDK semantics; do not assume separate SDK calls form an atomic transaction. A destructive account command must use the checked account's authorization. If the SDK acquires its default token asynchronously, use supported per-call headers after checking the session; a mutable global token or an earlier UI owner check does not bind the outgoing request.
verification: delay a challenge, replace the account or unmount, then complete it; no new command may target the replacement. Delay an entered email update/OTP, start cleanup, then finish it; cleanup must converge without resurrecting a removed session or discarding a valid replacement. Use the installed SDK to delay token acquisition, then verify the actual outgoing Authorization owner and real service effects with isolated accounts. Keep credentials out of test output.
boundaries: 2026-09-07, Supabase auth-js 2.112.3 source and controlled client regressions. Native persistence and real network interruption need separate physical/integration evidence.

entries.title: Auth bootstrap is not logout
entries.trigger: device registration cleanup compares a persisted owner with asynchronously restored Auth/profile state, and cleanup has durable server effects.
entries.mechanism: the UI actor is initially null; cleanup treats this as logout and revokes the still-valid session's device binding. Account reads continue working while push registration fails.
entries.prevention: wait for explicit Auth readiness before destructive cleanup. Use the restored session owner while profile data is pending; absence of a loaded profile does not establish logout. Keep the server's protection against delayed post-logout registration. Report OS permission separately from registration success; a server failure must not be described as an OS permission failure.
verification: defer bootstrap, restore the same owner, then exercise a real sign-out and account replacement. Assert no early cleanup and correct cleanup after an actual ownership change. Verify device-to-server registration after restart; mocked success cannot validate server revocation state.
boundaries: 2026-09-07, React 19.2, Expo Notifications 57.0.17 and Supabase JS 2.112.3. The failure mechanism also applies to other SDKs with asynchronous identity restoration and durable cleanup.

entries.title: A one-time proof can succeed before a command reports duplicate
entries.trigger: a managed request accepts a one-time CAPTCHA proof and starts an irreversible side effect, but its response times out before the client receives the outcome.
entries.mechanism: production `/recover` logged `user_recovery_requested` and then a 10-second `request_timeout`; the same request then reported `captcha_failed` with `timeout-or-duplicate`. Android displayed the final error even though the recovery email had arrived.
entries.prevention: distinguish only the provider's exact duplicate result when the client minted the proof immediately before that protected request. Continue to the authoritative verification step without automatically repeating the side effect. Keep every other CAPTCHA rejection fail-closed.
verification: regress the exact duplicate and a generic CAPTCHA rejection separately, then verify the provider-backed flow on the affected device. A code-entry screen cannot establish that email was delivered; successful OTP verification remains authoritative.
boundaries: 2026-09-08, Supabase Auth 2.196.0, Supabase JS 2.112.3 and Cloudflare Turnstile. The client keeps the supported managed recovery API and adds no custom transport or email endpoint.

entries.title: A collection limit and a per-request limit are different contracts
entries.trigger: a client loads metadata for a collection through an endpoint with a bounded ID list.
entries.mechanism: small accounts pass, but crossing the endpoint limit makes the whole metadata request fail. Deduplicating IDs alone does not bound the request or prove collection completeness.
entries.prevention: honor the endpoint's batch size, bound concurrency, preserve metadata identity, and stop later batches after cancellation or loss of eligibility. Separately inspect server row caps and pagination; successful metadata batching cannot recover omitted collection rows. Consume the owning query's cancellation and preserve its account between collection pages. Use stable unique cursors where supported so earlier deletions cannot shift remaining rows past an offset. A multi-request read still needs later refresh for concurrent changes; it is not a snapshot.
verification: zero, exact limit, limit plus one, duplicate IDs, failure between batches, owner replacement, and query cancellation. Verify the actual endpoint contract as well as client orchestration.
boundaries: 2026-09-07, Supabase functions-js 2.112.3 supports an AbortSignal; client regressions cover bounded sequential calls. Native fetch cancellation and service behavior require separate evidence.

entries.title: A missing response does not prove a failed command
entries.trigger: a command can commit server state before its response reaches the device.
entries.mechanism: retry duplicates a successful mutation, or the UI reports failure while the server retains committed data and later restore exposes inconsistent local metadata.
entries.prevention: use the existing command's idempotency and canonical outcome mechanism. Distinguish deterministic rejection from an unknown outcome. Preserve the minimum durable receipt needed to reconcile after process death; do not invent a generic retry transport. On the server, an empty recovery read can precede an in-flight commit. Keep registered candidate files until transactional adoption or the established delayed cleanup resolves their ownership. Never delete a potential canonical file solely because the mutation's HTTP response was lost. Repeated acknowledgment of a relationship command must preserve later revocation: use its original operation identity and current canonical outcome, without resurrecting a removed relationship. An unchanged user retry must retain that identity; a short server duplicate window is not a substitute. Canonical observation can beat the error response. Restore or clear only the draft still owned by that attempt, and preserve later edits when the canonical result arrives. For an account preference, keep saving feedback active during the authoritative read. Clear the command error only when a successful read no earlier than that attempt confirms the requested value; a failed or mismatching read retains the error. Reset a stale mutation error after later canonical confirmation so an unrelated future refresh failure cannot resurrect it.
verification: commit the command and drop its response, retry, then restart the client. Assert one canonical mutation and convergence of local state, UI and owned files. Repeat with actual rejection, a failed recovery read, a mismatching value, later confirmation and account replacement.
boundaries: 2026-09-08, including real Postgres/Storage commits with lost responses before and after commit plus TanStack Query 5.101.4 preference reconciliation. The exact receipt, adoption and cleanup protocol belongs to the adopting backend.

entries.title: Missing push receipts are unknown delivery outcomes
entries.trigger: a push provider accepts a message and exposes a later delivery-receipt lookup.
entries.mechanism: an omitted receipt ID was recorded as a final provider error. The provider later returned success, but the application had permanently stopped checking that ticket.
entries.prevention: distinguish accepted tickets, pending receipt lookups, explicit provider outcomes and actual device delivery. Retry missing receipt lookups using the existing bounded policy; never resend the push merely because its receipt is absent. Retain unknown status if the budget expires.
verification: partial response with success/error/missing IDs, missing then later success, stale lookup lease, exhausted retry budget and no outbox resend. Real device banner/badge acceptance is separate from inbox refresh and even an ok provider receipt.
boundaries: 2026-09-07, Expo Push Service contract and real omitted-then-ok receipt; Edge regressions and PostgreSQL lease/retry integration passed. No platform-specific delivery cause was proved.

entries.title: Object-info and directory-list names have different path scopes
entries.trigger: trusted code replaces a Storage directory listing with exact object metadata.
entries.mechanism: Supabase Storage `info(actor/work/file.jpg)` returned the full bucket-relative name, but publication compared it with only `file.jpg`. Every valid upload was classified as absent, cleaned up and rejected before download, while callers still using `list(actor/work)` succeeded.
entries.prevention: validate exact-object info against the full bucket-relative path. Compare directory-list entries with the basename only when the provider's list contract returns names relative to the queried directory. Preserve a focused regression when changing between those APIs.
verification: prove that the exact full path is accepted and its basename alone is rejected; then correlate the hosted info request, function outcome and subsequent download for one real upload.
boundaries: 2026-09-10, Supabase Storage/storage-js 2.112.3 and a hosted publication-command incident.

entries.title: Cached bytes do not prove that the origin can be restored
entries.trigger: a backend decides whether a canonical object needs repair by downloading its bytes.
entries.mechanism: a CDN returns a previously cached matching object after origin deletion, so an integrity check incorrectly skips repair. This also occurred with browser cacheControl set to zero.
entries.prevention: use the provider's supported origin-refresh option for authoritative integrity checks. Keep ordinary display caching separate. Do not treat a recent successful download or metadata row as proof that the origin currently retains the bytes, and do not invent a new transport.
verification: upload with runtime cache settings, warm the actual path, remove the origin, then compare the repair decision with a fresh origin read. Check matching/mismatched bytes, retry and exact fixture cleanup. CDN invalidation is not necessarily immediate after successful deletion.
boundaries: 2026-09-07, real Supabase hosted Storage and storage-js 2.112.3. Its cacheNonce download option is supported; other providers require their own documented mechanism.
